profileSections.heading: A personal and professional story
profileSections.text: On her Sunshine Pediatrics biography, Cynthia Bui connects a local beginning with a return home: she grew up in Irvine and says her own pediatrician inspired her career. After eight years on the East Coast, she returned to Southern California for pediatric residency at UCI–CHOC. Her account also describes research in newborn brain development and pediatric sports medicine, plus a medical trip to Vietnam where she provided primary care to underserved communities and worked on child environmental-health research. These are her published reflections, not a report of patient outcomes.

profileSections.heading: A personal and professional story
profileSections.text: Jiyeon Kim's profile describes a childhood across multiple countries and an appreciation for each family's background and values. It recounts earlier work teaching and mentoring pediatric residents in research at the University of Illinois College of Medicine at Peoria, alongside community advocacy. Outside work, she says she enjoys learning Japanese, exploring new foods and Pilates, and running family 5Ks (or “slow jogging”). This is her biography's account; current academic appointments or advocacy roles are not implied.

profileSections.heading: A personal and professional story
profileSections.text: Christine Kornu's story moves from San Diego to practice in Dallas and back to Southern California. Her profile describes work in both a children's academic hospital and a community clinic, including coordination of the Reach Out and Read early-literacy program. She also notes medical mission work in Thailand, Nepal and Mexico and leadership with youth organizations. Her current practice biography says she is beginning a new pediatrics practice in Irvine; this does not claim outcomes or independent license confirmation.

profileSections.heading: A personal and professional story
profileSections.text: Mary Anne Galang-Lomboy traces her interest in pediatrics to growing up around medicine—her mother was a nurse—and helping care for three younger brothers. She says she enjoys meeting children at different stages of life and working with the whole family. In describing her approach, she emphasizes listening and taking time for a child's feelings. These are her published reflections, not promises about any particular patient's experience or outcome.
